hormuz_disruption.label: Iran / Hormuz Disruption
hormuz_disruption.last_note: Iran closed the Strait on June 20 citing Israeli ceasefire violations, directly reversing the June 17 Versailles MOU that called for immediate reopening — the disruption thesis remains live but diplomatic fragility has increased materially rather than resolved.

stagflation_regime.label: Stagflation Regime
stagflation_regime.last_note: May 2026 CPI accelerated to 4.2 percent from 3.8 percent in April driven by energy, the Fed held at 3.50 to 3.75 percent, and markets now price one hike by October — stagflation regime is fully intact with no rate-cut pathway in sight.

ai_bubble_risk.label: AI Bubble Risk Q4 2026
ai_bubble_risk.last_note: Statista confirmed hyperscaler capex tracking up to $725 billion in 2026 while big tech has already issued $100 billion in bonds to fund AI infrastructure, raising debt-sustainability concerns that validate bubble-risk monitoring heading into Q4.

gold_supercycle.label: Gold Supercycle
gold_supercycle.last_note: WTI crude fell to a 3.5-month low on Thursday pressuring energy inflation expectations, and even if Hormuz fully reopens it will likely take months for the global energy crisis to ease, leaving gold caught between a ceasefire relief bid and persistent safe-haven demand — the 22 percent drawdown from the $5,500 high remains a structural caution flag.

copper_deficit.label: Structural Copper Deficit
copper_deficit.last_note: WTO data confirms a 95 percent reduction in crude oil shipments through Hormuz and the UAE state oil company estimates full flows will not resume until 2027, sustaining commodity supply-chain stress that underpins the structural copper deficit thesis.

nuclear_renaissance.label: Nuclear Renaissance
nuclear_renaissance.last_note: Meta and Microsoft signed agreements for nuclear capacity for AI data centers, the DOE awarded a $900 million HALEU enrichment contract and $800 million for SMR construction, while uranium spot holds near $85 per pound in a tight range — structural demand signals remain unbroken.

ALAB.note: Q1 2026 revenue of $308 million up 93 percent YoY confirms the AI connectivity thesis is operationally intact, but ALAB at P/E 99 remains priced for execution perfection with Q2 results not due until August 11 — valuation is the lingering disqualifier.

POWL.note: Hyperscaler capex tracking up to $725 billion in 2026 with Microsoft carrying an $80 billion Azure backlog it cannot fulfill due to power constraints validates the data center electrical infrastructure thesis, but POWL at P/E 43 has fully priced the cycle with no new catalyst.

MOD.note: GPU-heavy AI facilities require higher rack densities and direct-to-chip liquid cooling as foundational infrastructure, which supports the MOD thermal management thesis, but negative FCF of minus $101 million remains a disqualifying quality flag and no near-term FCF inflection is confirmed.

GFS.note: GFS 2026 Investor Day confirmed record design wins, a 50 percent rise in design wins, and a European sovereign chip flow targeting aerospace and defense — the CHIPS Act foundry thesis is broadening into defense and AI silicon photonics, which is incrementally positive thesis drift but no blockbuster contract catalyst has landed.

CRDO.note: CRDO completed the DustPhotonics acquisition in late May 2026 expanding silicon photonics capabilities, and fiscal Q4 2026 expectations exceeded 150 percent YoY revenue growth — the AI connectivity thesis remains the strongest in its peer group.

ARM.note: Hyperscalers are now funding AI capex with debt as capex exceeds internal cash generation at 45 to 57 percent of revenue — any capex deceleration signal hits ARM royalty growth directly and P/E 143 with $750 million FCF leaves zero margin for error in a higher-for-longer rate environment.

S.note: SentinelOne issued lackluster guidance, cut 8 percent of its workforce, and took a $25 million restructuring charge — the thesis has drifted from pure growth-at-scale to an AI-pivot restructuring story, which is a meaningful character change at current valuation.

ZS.note: Zscaler maintains the strongest FCF in cybersecurity at $1.1B but remains rated AVOID — the valuation at P/E 28.37 does not screen as expensive yet the growth deceleration thesis and intensifying platform competition have not resolved in ZS favor.

AXON.note: AXON Q1 2026 revenue of $807 million up 34 percent with ARR at $1.5 billion growing 35 percent, AI products up over 700 percent, and full-year FCF guided to approximately $450 million — the prior AVOID call based on $63 million FCF is now broken and thesis drift is STRONGLY POSITIVE, warranting immediate re-evaluation to WATCH or BUY.

ISRG.note: Intuitive Surgical has zero debt, $4.5B cash, 23% revenue growth, and $2.3B FCF making it a genuine compounder, but at 36x forward earnings and 29.4% below highs the surgical robotics moat thesis is unchanged — the drift is purely valuation-related, not fundamental, and the stock remains a hold-not-add until the multiple contracts further.

RXRX.note: Recursion Pharmaceuticals has revenue growth of minus 56.1%, is burning $178M in FCF with negative operating margins of minus 1985%, and is 55.2% below its 52-week high — the original AI drug discovery thesis has collapsed as clinical pipeline progress has not justified the technology premium and this is now a capital destruction story with no near-term catalyst.

JEDI.note: The drone and modern warfare rearmament thesis is structurally intact given the Hormuz crisis has accelerated defense technology procurement, but at 25% below highs and with no fundamental data available for an ETF wrapper this remains a theme trade that requires a defined technical base before adding risk.

CWAN.note: Clearwater Analytics has 74.4% revenue growth and $160M FCF which is operationally compelling, but analyst targets of $24.47 to $24.55 against the current $24.35 price provide virtually zero upside consensus — at PEG of 10.24 and EV/EBITDA of 73.69 the institutional fintech thesis is fully priced with no margin of safety.

GRAB.note: Grab at $3.30 with $6.5B cash, 23.5% revenue growth, and PEG of 0.87 is the most asymmetric deep value setup in the portfolio on a pure fundamentals basis, but the stock is 50.2% below highs and the Southeast Asia super-app monetization thesis requires a specific catalyst such as a buyback announcement or profitability upgrade to unlock value — thesis intact, no trigger yet.

VRT.note: Vertiv is a direct beneficiary of the above 1 trillion dollar 2026 data center capex cycle with power constraint urgency confirmed by the Microsoft 80 billion dollar Azure backlog, but stretched valuation demands flawless execution at a time when macro uncertainty is high.

MU.note: MU led the chip stock rally on June 15 on Iran deal optimism and structural AI memory demand is intact given that memory cost inflation drove data center capex higher in Q1 2026, but the stock is cyclical and a stagflation-driven consumer slowdown could compress DRAM pricing outside the AI data center vertical.

AMD.note: AMD surged on June 15 following an analyst upgrade and the Iran deal catalyst, with the company announcing up to 2 billion pounds in UK AI investment and the MEXT memory optimization acquisition signaling a serious data center strategy, but the stock at 548.80 dollars trades at a premium that assumes continued hyperscaler GPU wallet share gains from Nvidia.
